protocol: read-only: reuse frozen 5-truck test split and saved M1.2 artifacts; no training/refitting/tuning; test used only for evaluation; trip-level resampling (not telemetry rows)
analysis_frame: conditional on the five frozen test trucks (truck_001, truck_004, truck_017, truck_020, truck_028); does NOT establish population-level generalization across trucks

full_operational.basis: validation MAE (M1.2) — test data not used

telematics_only.basis: validation MAE (M1.2) — test data not used

pooled_paired_delta.sign_convention: delta = MAE_telematics_only - MAE_full_operational; positive => full-operational has lower error (better)

bootstrap.method: trip-clustered percentile bootstrap; resample the 96 test trips with replacement, jointly for both models; 95% percentile interval
bootstrap.note: estimates uncertainty conditional on these five test trucks; does NOT establish population-level generalization across trucks

variance_decomposition.note: 5-truck sample: truck-level variance component is descriptive and unstable; a formal ANOVA ICC is NOT reported because n=5 trucks is too small for a defensible between-truck random-effect estimate. No causal interpretation.

limitations: Synthetic telemetry: results are pipeline validation, not observed real-world Indian truck telemetry.
Only five test trucks: truck-level estimates (tail, variance decomposition, macro) are descriptive and unstable; not population estimates.
Trip-clustered bootstrap resamples the 96 test trips and therefore reflects uncertainty conditional on these five trucks only.
Repeated trips of the same truck are not fully independent; we mitigate this by resampling at the trip level rather than rows.
49T class is represented by a single truck; no class-level generalization claims are made.
